long_biography.plain_text:
Reece trained as a chartered accountant after studying economics at Cambridge. By the time INEOS recruited him in 2000, he was a PricewaterhouseCoopers partner with a specialised chemicals practice. That combination placed him in charge of the young group's finances as it pursued acquisitions; he later became a minority shareholder and remains among its three co-owners.

His most revealing chapter came during the 2008 credit crisis, after INEOS had borrowed heavily to acquire BP's chemicals businesses. Negotiations with lenders secured temporary covenant relief, but also exposed weaknesses in the group's investor relationships. INEOS subsequently made regular communication with its financiers part of its operating discipline. Reece continues to represent the ownership group at board level, including as a Manchester United director.
